summary: Assistance requested: rollback plan for hybrid optimizer stack causing tenant spikes
description: Issue summary: Customer reported sudden 95th/99th percentile latency spikes and increased 5xx rates after recent tenant-scoped optimizer profile rollout that layered both KV-prefetch and an aggressive quantization profile for long-context requests. Impact: Multiple production customers using HydroCare's private deployment experienced request failures and degraded response times impacting critical patient-facing workflows. Environment: Private deployment connected via VPC, tenant pinned to a mixed optimizer profile (prefetch + quant aggressive + larger batch targets) on serving pool redwood-prod-us-east. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a mixed short/long prompt workload using the galen-13b-quant model pinned to tenant-optimizer-profile. 2) Observe sustained tail latency growth after ~20 minutes of mixed traffic and occasional GPU memory OOM or eviction events in logs. 3) Reproduce spikes using the customer's traffic replay (provided) against a staging clone of the serving pool. Observed behavior: 95p/99p latencies increase by 2.8x, occasional 502/504 errors, and eviction traces showing heavy KV cache churn. Expected behavior: Stable tail latency within SLA, no OOMs or evictions under the expected load. Initial hypothesis: Interaction between KV-prefetch eviction heuristics and the aggressive quant profile is increasing memory pressure and causing frequent cache thrashing; combined with larger batching targets, this produces longer process queues and timeouts. Also possible kernel selection mismatch increasing per-step CPU/GPU overhead for certain sequence-length mixes.

investigation_notes: Checked serving logs: frequent kv_cache evict events starting at 2026-03-11 22:15 UTC coincident with rollout. Evictions correlate with increase in GPU memory allocations and kernel fallback logs.
Heap snapshots show memory spike patterns when mixed short+long sequence requests arrive; batching heuristic aggregated incompatible sequences increasing KV working set.
Profiler traces indicate fallback to non-optimized kernels for certain attention blocks under the aggressive quant profile, increasing CPU-to-GPU synchronization and latency.
Staging replay reproduced 95p/99p latency increase after enabling both KV-prefetch and the aggressive quant profile; disabling either reduced tail by ~40-55%.
workaround: Applied temporary routing change to divert 60% of HydroCare traffic to a conservative profile variant and reduced tenant batch target from 64 to 24. This restored nominal tail latency within SLA for the duration of the maintenance window. No full rollback yet; change implemented via config flag toggle and traffic-split policy.
next_steps: Run a controlled rollback during maintenance window: sequence - 1) snapshot current tenant optimizer profile, 2) toggle off KV-prefetch feature flag for tenant, 3) revert quant profile to prior conservative snapshot, 4) reduce batch_target for tenant to 24, 5) monitor 1/5/15 min SLO dashboards and logs.
Prepare rollback playbook with exact CLI/API commands and feature-flag toggles (see related_confluence_pages).
Coordinate with customer to run a smoke test suite using their replay file immediately after rollback and verify no functional regressions in outputs.
If rollback successful, prepare postmortem and blocker list to harden rollout gating (add preflight staging simulation and memory pressure checks).
If rollback incomplete or causes new regressions, escalate to runtime engineers and consider temporary capacity scale-up to avoid timeouts while debugging.
Follow-up: schedule a joint reconciliation session to design a safer staged rollout path for the mixed optimizer stacking scenario (prefer stepwise enablement with shadow testing).
